 BYU, Utah remain locked in place in latest College Football Playoff rankings
 Updated - Nov. 17, 2026 at 10:04 p.m.
 | Posted - Nov. 17, 2026 at 7:55 p.m. 
 Josh Furlong KSL    
  
  
  
 Save Story SALT LAKE CITY — As Utah football players and coaches gathered together at the program's football facility, prepared to embark on a trip to the airport for a flight to Tucson, Arizona, Friday afternoon, the FAA grounded all planes for just the third time in the country's history.
 There were little answers as Utah officials attempted to figure out a path to Arizona before a 5:30 p.m. kickoff the next day.
 Once the ground stop was lifted, the only option available to the team was to fly out the morning of the game — an uncommon situation that complicated the day's events, even with the game pushed back three hours to accommodate Utah's delayed arrival.
 Utah's health and nutrition staff used certain measures to help the team, but the overarching message within the program was "no excuses." Regardless of the weekend's events, Utah coaches and players weren't going to let it define how they performed on the field against a tough Arizona team intent on upsetting the No. 2 team in the country.
 So when Devon Dampier hit a streaking Creed Whittemore in the final minutes of the game on a 70-yard game-winning touchdown pass to overcome Arizona's late go-ahead score, Utah fully realized its mantra to maintain an undefeated season.
 "Our culture is no excuses; we live by it," Dampier said after the game. "That was the mindset when we came out here. No one's gonna feel sorry for us if we would have lost this game, so that was just kind of the mindset. No one's gonna feel bad for us that we had to find a way around this to get here and play on the same day. So it was just the mindset: come out there and let's go ball."
 That mindset has treated Utah well all season and has the Utes as one of only two remaining teams with an undefeated record. With two games left in the regular season — two games Utah is favored to win — the team is a near lock for a College Football Playoff berth in Morgan Scalley's first season as a head coach.
 On Tuesday, the College Football Playoff selection committee kept Utah as the No. 2 team in the country, giving the Utes a potential first-round bye in the playoffs should the rankings remain on Selection Sunday.
 If so, Utah would likely have its choice of playing in the Fiesta Bowl (Dec. 30) or the Rose Bowl (Jan. 1), assuming Georgia maintains its No. 1 spot and chose the Peach Bowl (Jan. 1) — a no-brainer given it would be a home game for the team.
 Utah needs just one win over the final two games to lock up a spot in the Big 12 championship game and has a 98% chance of making the playoff , according to ESPN analytics. Those same analytics give Utah a 14% chance to make it to the national championship game and a 5.2% chance to win it all.
 Selection committee chairman Hunter Yurachek said the committee has a "pretty clear understanding" of who they see as the No. 1 and No. 2 teams, with the six or seven teams behind Utah having a "razor thin" margin in comparison.
 "Those are some of the closest comparisons and most comprehensive and heated discussions we had in the room over the past two days," Yurachek said.
 Joining Utah from the Big 12 in the rankings for another week is No. 10 BYU, who stayed put for another week after a win over Baylor on Saturday. The Cougars get some love by being above a hot Wake Forest team, who is just one spot behind BYU.
 Yurachek said the biggest reason why BYU remains above Wake Forest is the win over Notre Dame, who dropped a spot this week in the rankings.
 "Wake Forest doesn't have the dame type of win on their resume right now," he said. "That's going to be the separation between those two teams."
 The Big 12 has three other teams ranked this week, including No. 12 Texas Tech, No. 19 Arizona and No. 20 Houston. Like Utah, Texas Tech remains the only other team i the conference to control its destiny for a Big 12 title game appearance.
 Despite losing to Arizona, the Wildcats moved up four spots in the rankings, which helps Utah's resume and gives the Big 12 another quality team included in the rankings.
